title: Morphisms into a disjoint union of copies of the base are clopen decompositions
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ a set. Let $U_E=\coprod_{e\in E}U$ be the coproduct of copies of $U$ indexed by $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with coprojections $\iota_e:U\to U_E$, and let $\pi:U_E\to U$ be the morphism with $\pi\circ\iota_e=\mathrm{id}_U$ for all $e\in E$; write $V_e=\iota_e(U)\subseteq U_E$. Let $s:W\to U$ be a morphism of schemes. Call a family $(W_e)_{e\in E}$ of open subsets of $W$ an *$E$-indexed clopen decomposition* of $W$ if the $W_e$ are pairwise disjoint and $W=\bigcup_{e\in E}W_e$ (then each $W_e$ is also closed); regard each $W_e$ as an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] with inclusion $j_e:W_e\to W$. Then: (a) for every morphism $f:W\to U_E$ with $\pi\circ f=s$, the family $(f^{-1}(V_e))_{e\in E}$ is an $E$-indexed clopen decomposition of $W$, and $f\circ j_e=\iota_e\circ s\circ j_e$ on $W_e=f^{-1}(V_e)$ for every $e\in E$; (b) for every $E$-indexed clopen decomposition $(W_e)_{e\in E}$ of $W$ there is exactly one morphism $f:W\to U_E$ with $\pi\circ f=s$ and $f^{-1}(V_e)=W_e$ for all $e\in E$. Hence $f\mapsto(f^{-1}(V_e))_{e\in E}$ is a bijection from the set of $U$-morphisms $W\to U_E$ onto the set of $E$-indexed clopen decompositions of $W$, equivalently onto the set of maps $\varphi:|W|\to E$ all of whose fibres are open ($W_e=\varphi^{-1}(e)$). (c) For $e_0\in E$ the morphism $\iota_{e_0}\circ s$ corresponds to the decomposition with $W_{e_0}=W$ and $W_e=\varnothing$ for $e\neq e_0$ (the constant map with value $e_0$). For $E=\varnothing$, $U_\varnothing$ is the empty scheme, and a $U$-morphism $W\to U_\varnothing$ exists (and is then unique) if and only if $W$ is empty.
